history.text: The NWA was formed as a governing body, and the title became the alliance's property.
Billy Goelz was recognized as the governing body's champion, and earlier Iowa champions were retroactively recognized.
Leroy McGuirk defeated Billy Goelz, unifying the Iowa and Los Angeles versions.
related: National Wrestling Association World Junior Heavyweight Championship (Los Angeles version)

history.text: The title was vacated after McGuirk retired following a car accident that left him blind.
Danny McShain defeated Verne Gagne to win the title.
McShain defeated Rito Romero, unifying the Los Angeles version into the NWA title.
related: NWA World Junior Heavyweight Championship (Los Angeles version)

history.text: Wrestling Pro was recognized as champion only in the GCCW territory, not by the NWA.
Steve Keirn was recognized by NJPW and some NWA territories but not the NWA; that version was later renamed.
Ron Starr was recognized by the NWA as champion over Steve Keirn, the international champion.
The title split into two lineages, with The Cobra recognized by the NWA and Les Thornton recognized by Georgia Championship Wrestling.
Jim Crockett Promotions awarded the title to Hector Guerrero after claiming he won a tournament, a disputed version.
NJPW left the NWA, and NWA vice president Shohei Baba recognized Denny Brown as the official champion.
The championship was abandoned after Atlantic Coast Wrestling closed.
Wrestle Yume Factory revived the championship, with Masayoshi Motegi as the first champion under its banner.
The J-Crown tournament unified eight junior heavyweight titles, with The Great Sasuke as the first J-Crown Champion.
The J-Crown was dissolved, and the component titles were returned to their home promotions, with the NWA title left vacant.
Craig Classic vacated the title in protest, and Zero1 declared him the real champion instead.
related: New Wrestling Alliance World Junior Heavyweight Championship (Pro Wrestling Zero1)

history.text: The NWA re-established its working relationship with NJPW.
Billy Corgan's company bought the NWA and its championships, and the title was vacated; ownership took effect October 1, 2017.
Homicide won the vacant title at the Crockett Cup, ending the vacancy that began in 2017.
Spencer Slade was stripped, and Hayden Backlund won the vacant title in a four-way match.
